subject.title: Npm-valid package scopes with dots/underscores cannot map to ClawHub publishers

question: Should the shipped npm-compatible dot and underscore publisher handles with exact normalized package-scope matching be the permanent ClawHub ownership contract?
rationale: The runtime behavior is deployed, but publisher identity grammar determines publishing authorization and repository policy requires explicit durable intent for ownership boundaries.

options.title: Ratify exact npm-scope identities
options.body: Keep the shipped grammar and exact equality rule, then document the complete authorization and compatibility invariant in the ownership specification.

options.title: Design explicit scope aliases
options.body: Retain current compatibility while designing a first-class alias model across publishing, routing, transfers, installs, and recovery.

options.title: Plan scoped package renames
options.body: Deprecate these identities only with an explicit migration and package-transition plan that avoids breaking existing publishers.

recommendation.title: Ratify exact npm-scope identities
recommendation.body: Keep the shipped grammar and exact equality rule, then document the complete authorization and compatibility invariant in the ownership specification.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen authored both the focused shipped fix and the issue's security-policy alternatives.
